thread:
deploy-bot: [ALERT] Multiple pods in ap-northeast1 experiencing GPU device plugin bind failures after rolling kubelet upgrade. 02:00 UTC.

sara: saw a spike in `device-plugin` errors and a bunch of pods stuck Pending with `BindDevice: failed` in the events. This started right after the 1.28.3->1.29.0 kubelet rollout last night.

ming: can you paste the device-plugin logs? I rolled back one node and it recovered.

oliver: logs from a bad node: 
```
I0401 01:58:12.345 device-plugin.go:212] Registered device plugin for nvidia.com/gpu
E0401 01:58:12.346 device-plugin.go:317] Bind failed: VF index 5 not found for pod ml/worker-7
E0401 01:58:12.347 kubelet.go:88] failed to allocate device: device not found
```
Looks like VF indices are different on nodes now.

rhea: we also see the vf numbering in sysfs changed ordering after the kernel module from vendor had an ABI bump that the new kubelet interprets differently. Vendor announced a driver package yesterday that flips how SR-IOV VFs are enumerated on hotplug.

ming: ugh. So device plugin asks for VF #5 but kernel presents the GPU mapping as #6 etc. That causes BindDevice to fail -> scheduler thinks node can't fulfill request -> pod is requeued -> binpacking becomes noisy since many pods bounce.

ops-bot: autoscaler: scaled up 12 nodes in ap-northeast1 between 02:05-02:20 due to pending pods. Scale-down in progress now.

sara: cost hit: preliminary billing shows ~900 USD extra for the scale up window. Also pod churn caused GPU fragmentation (lots of nodes with 1-2 placed pods instead of filling GPUs).

oliver: immediate mitigation options I see:
1) pin device-plugin to old behaviour by setting env var to map by PCI ID instead of index (config change),
2) roll kubelet back where nodes are healthy,
3) update vendor driver ASAP to stable enumerations and coordinate with node reboot (disruptive).

rhea: option 1 is the fastest low-risk. We can change dp configmap to prefer device UUID mapping (fallback to index) and restart plugin daemonset. That should make binds stable across the inconsistent VF numbering.

ming: will that avoid eviction churn too? Scheduler still thinks capacity is limited due to pods in CrashLoopPending maybe. We should also pause the autoscaler to avoid more overprovision while we fix mapping.

ops-bot: autoscaler pause initiated for ap-northeast1 at 02:28 UTC.

sara: patch for device-plugin config applied to one node pool (canary) at 02:35. Observed binds go from 92% failure -> 4% failure on canary. Nice.

oliver: yay. Next: rollout to remaining nodes in that AZ, and coordinate with node-image team to avoid reintroducing the kernel/driver combo that reorders VFs. I'll open TICKET-5012 for vendor coordination.

rhea: follow-ups:
- add an admission webhook guard that rejects pods requesting explicit VF indices (we prefer UUIDs) (rhea).
- add a scheduler predicate to prefer packing by device UUID equivalence groups so we avoid cross-node VF mapping surprises (ming).
- update launch templates to pin kernel+driver versions until vendor confirms stable enumeration (sara).

ming: long-term: need to add an integration test that does a driver hotpatch and validates device-plugin binds and pod placement. Filing TEST-2012.

ops-bot: final status (02:54 UTC): device bind failures back to baseline. Autoscaler unpaused at 03:10 UTC after monitoring window. TICKET-5012 and TEST-2012 created. Keeping incident open for postmortem.

sara: postmortem items include cost impact, scheduler packing regression (pods scattered due to transient bind failures), and an action to add a small backoff window before autoscaler reacts to bind failures (to avoid scale storms).

oliver: thanks all. We'll coordinate vendor call tomorrow 09:00 local. :phone:
